The customer collection spine

Tenant→Service→Service version→Run→Attempt→Artifact

The Run keeps exact version/release pins and validated input. Events explain its lifecycle; Artifact receipts identify private result bytes; usage observes records; outbox/audit preserve admission and authorization evidence.

The Marketplace preview boundary

Reviewed candidate→Draft contract→Governed sample→Bounded download

Preview filtering is on stored governed sample rows, not live full-provider data. A sample download/enquiry does not create a Service, Run, entitlement, payment or provider Filter job. Private M9/M10 evidence is a separate lane.

Identities — six meanings, not one

“Identity” can mean a customer person, company, request actor or PostgreSQL execution principal. Keeping these separate is essential for Tenant isolation and safe handover.

IdentityStored / resolved fromMeaning and boundary
Customer personusers.idThe human account. One identity is not itself a workspace.
Company/workspacetenants.id / display_name + tenant_user_accessOwns customer business resources. Workspace name comes from persisted Tenant display_name, not the catalogue.
Authenticated request actorBrowser session or Dhumi API keyAuthentication resolves User/key, Tenant, workspace access and scopes. Raw tokens/verifiers are never atlas data.
Database connection identityEnvironment-specific dhumi_dev_*_login / dhumi_test_*_loginLOGIN opens a connection. NOINHERIT and explicit membership keep capability use deliberate.
Database capabilityEight fixed NOLOGIN dhumi_* rolesSET LOCAL ROLE selects the permitted repository workflow for one transaction.
Schema/function ownerdhumi_owner (NOLOGIN)Owns DDL and controlled SECURITY DEFINER functions. Not an ordinary API/worker login.
Role + transaction Tenant + grants + RLS + guarded functions

Tenant seams use SELECT set_config('app.tenant_id', $1, true) with a validated UUID. This is transaction-local and resets after commit/rollback. An unset Tenant helper returns NULL; require_tenant_context() rejects missing context. The Tenant is resolved by authentication, not accepted as arbitrary customer input.

FORCE RLS makes the owner subject to row policies for ordinary access; it does not stop superusers/BYPASSRLS. RLS does not replace grants, fixed search paths or constraints, and table-wide operations such as TRUNCATE are not covered. Global private tables without RLS are not automatically public. PostgreSQL 18 RLS, SET ROLE, object/column grants.

PUBLIC is not a login

PUBLIC means all roles, not an application account. Raw function grants are shown as observed; the installed reject_marketplace_qualification_packet_contract_mutation() trigger has PUBLIC EXECUTE in this snapshot. A trigger-returning function is not a normal HTTP operation. Never assume all functions have PUBLIC revoked without inspecting the actual ACL.

Security-function interpretation

SECURITY INVOKER uses caller privileges; SECURITY DEFINER uses the function owner's privileges. Owner policies on forced-RLS tables, restricted EXECUTE, fixed trusted search_path and input/fence checks must be understood together. Use the exact source and tests before widening a grant. PostgreSQL CREATE FUNCTION security guidance.

Transactions — what commits together

Sixteen compact walkthroughs explain the existing database boundaries. PostgreSQL owns business state; external storage, queue and provider calls are not included in a database commit.

Atomic inside PostgreSQL ≠ distributed exactly once

Idempotency, unique receipts, row locks, expected revisions and Attempt fences protect defined database effects. Outbox delivery can repeat. Provider ambiguity requires reconciliation, not automatic billable resubmission. Never infer a paid Marketplace execution entitlement from a cost-hold row.

Walkthrough 01 · All eight capability seams

Shared transaction boundary

runTransaction → SET LOCAL ROLE → optional set_config(app.tenant_id, UUID, true)

  1. Acquire one pool client; BEGIN; install the fixed capability role.
  2. For Tenant seams, validate the UUID and set transaction-local app.tenant_id before work.
  3. Execute repository work; COMMIT on success. On any error, ROLLBACK; destroy the connection if rollback itself fails.
Boundary / failure behavior

Role/Tenant context is local to the transaction, not a permanent pooled-session setting. Helpers use plain BEGIN; they do not independently guarantee SERIALIZABLE isolation.

Walkthrough 02 · dhumi_identity

Signup, session and refresh

withIdentityTransaction

  1. Signup claims operation idempotency and creates User, Tenant/workspace, owner membership, legal evidence, audit and outbox in one database operation.
  2. Successful sign-in locks/rechecks identity and workspace access, then records the session/refresh generation and sign-in audit.
  3. Refresh locks token/session state. Rotation consumes a generation; detected reuse revokes the family in the same locked transaction.
Boundary / failure behavior

Password verification/hashing and HTTP cookie/token response generation are application work. Identity has a dedicated pre-Tenant authority; ordinary customer table access must not bypass authentication.

Walkthrough 03 · dhumi_customer_api

Create/revoke Dhumi API keys

withTenantTransaction

  1. Creation couples the key verifier/scopes, idempotency response envelope and creation audit.
  2. Revocation locks the Tenant key, records the lifecycle change, audit and schema-v2 invalidation outbox event.
  3. The janitor later destroys only due recovery envelopes through its separate bounded seam.
Boundary / failure behavior

Key material/envelope cryptography happens in application composition; verifier/envelope columns are not part of the key list response. Delivery of invalidation messages is asynchronous.

Walkthrough 04 · dhumi_admission

Save a Service

withAdmissionTenantTransaction

  1. Claim/replay Service-creation idempotency against the authenticated Tenant.
  2. Recheck approved Template/version and persist the saved name plus immutable validated configuration version.
  3. Complete durable replay and audit atomically. Pin checks reject a version belonging to another Template.
Boundary / failure behavior

A catalogue pointer update does not modify this existing Service version. Creating a Service is not a provider submission.

Walkthrough 05 · dhumi_admission

Admit a Run

withAdmissionTenantTransaction

  1. Claim actor/operation idempotency; lock the selected Tenant Service; validate input against its pinned contract.
  2. Bind Service/Template/adapter/mapping/commercial/launch/feature identities and the permitted cost estimate. A shared-scraper pin resolves its immutable operation contract and must pass per-mapping commercial capacity.
  3. Persist the queued Run, accepted event, provider cost hold, audit, jobs.execute outbox and replay response in the admission transaction.
Boundary / failure behavior

No provider HTTP work is performed by this database admission. The shared path fails closed unless its released adapter identity, enabled mapping, approved immutable commercial evidence, input/record caps, daily/concurrent limits and cost ceiling all match. A cost hold is not Marketplace payment entitlement, and installed shared functions do not publish Target or enable the default-off worker flag.

Walkthrough 06 · dhumi_outbox_dispatcher

Publish a durable job command

withOutboxDispatcherTransaction

  1. Claim a bounded due job-topic batch with an expiring claim token.
  2. Send the queue message after the claim transaction commits.
  3. Mark publication only with the matching claim token. Crashes between send and mark can redeliver the command.
Boundary / failure behavior

Database commit and queue publish are not one distributed transaction. Assume at-least-once delivery; Attempt fences and idempotent lifecycle writes defend against duplicate execution effects.

Walkthrough 07 · dhumi_job_manager

Claim and execute / poll

withJobManagerTenantTransaction

  1. Claim an Attempt with its database lease/fence and resolve the exact adapter code, semantic version and artifact digest. Shared-scraper execution additionally resolves the operation contract and protected plan pinned to the Run.
  2. Perform authorized provider/storage operations outside the database transaction.
  3. Persist protected continuation and bounded polling status/deadline/backoff/failures under the still-owned fence; renew/finish only the owned Attempt.
Boundary / failure behavior

Redis and queue ownership are not authority. SQL functions do not themselves make Bright Data calls. The shared router accepts only registered exact identities, and its runtime flag remains default-off until deliberately enabled and regressed. A timeout or ambiguous POST is not permission to automatically submit again.

Walkthrough 08 · dhumi_job_manager / dhumi_operator

Reconcile ambiguity / controlled DLQ recovery

Tenant worker seam / private operator seam

  1. Inspect expired/ambiguous submission evidence and existing Artifacts before deciding what can be completed.
  2. Schedule a durable jobs.reconcile command instead of blindly repeating jobs.execute.
  3. Controlled DLQ recovery validates the original authoritative outbox event and de-duplicates recovery intent; reconciliation gets its own fence.
Boundary / failure behavior

Reconciliation reads a stored continuation or retained bytes where possible. Recovery must not manufacture new provider submission authority. Terminal Runs are not reopened merely because the queue redelivers.

Walkthrough 09 · dhumi_admission

Cancel or explicitly retry

withAdmissionTenantTransaction

  1. Cancellation locks the Tenant Run and admits a de-duplicated request/event/outbox command; the worker applies a permitted transition.
  2. Retry locks an eligible failed source and rejects wrong lineage or unresolved ambiguous execution.
  3. An accepted retry creates a new Run with source lineage and its own admission evidence; it never mutates the original into a new attempt.
Boundary / failure behavior

Cancel is best-effort, not a promise that the provider cancels/refunds. Explicit retry may be a new billable submission when enabled and authorized.

Walkthrough 10 · dhumi_result_recorder / dhumi_job_manager

Store results and complete success

Result-recorder Tenant transaction / fenced worker completion

  1. Privately store raw bytes and validated normalized bytes; register immutable Artifact receipts with exact checksums/byte/record counts.
  2. Require the validated normalized Artifact for the exact Run/Attempt before marking success.
  3. Fenced success/reconciliation finalization records or exactly reuses usage, transitions the Run and finishes the Attempt transactionally.
Boundary / failure behavior

Object upload and PostgreSQL commit are not a single atomic resource. A ready Run is based on validated stored evidence, not a provider UI success percentage. All-error/mixed-error outcomes follow the strict failure policy.

Walkthrough 11 · dhumi_customer_api

Authorize raw / normalized result

withTenantTransaction (lookup and audited recheck)

  1. Require authenticated results:read; Tenant lookup hides another Tenant's Run; require public_status=ready.
  2. Choose normalized+validated (default) or raw+durable, rejecting missing/expired receipts safely.
  3. After storage authorization, recheck the same Artifact/ready Run in the audit INSERT and record representation before returning the signed response.
Boundary / failure behavior

Signing/storage is outside the lookup transaction. Links are short-lived and private object_key is stripped from the public payload. Signing and auditing are not one distributed transaction.

Walkthrough 12 · dhumi_customer_api

Browse and query a governed stored sample

Customer-safe preview projection

  1. Resolve the active unexpired governed sample and approved dictionary through the restricted preview function.
  2. Load/verify bounded private source bytes and evaluate allowed filters/projection against that stored sample.
  3. Keep masked fields masked/non-filterable under policy; expose only allowlisted public metadata/rows.

Filtering preview rows is local and zero-provider-call; counts are sample matches, not live full-dataset matches. HTTP currently supports flat rule groups; service-level nested support is not a promise of a released HTTP contract.

Walkthrough 13 · dhumi_customer_api

Materialize a bounded sample download

Reserve → private storage work → complete (separate Tenant transactions)

  1. Reserve exact idempotency, field/filter projection, format, record count and checksum under rate/ceiling limits.
  2. Upload/sign masked JSON or spreadsheet-safe CSV outside the reservation transaction.
  3. Recheck the source/version and complete authorization+audit; on failure confirm guarded failed state before cleanup. Preserve uncertain objects for operator reconciliation.
Boundary / failure behavior

JSON is lossless for the allowed masked projection; dangerous CSV cells are neutralized for spreadsheet viewing. This is not a full export, purchase, entitlement, or unmasking operation.

Walkthrough 14 · dhumi_operator

Source sample ingestion and deletion

withOperatorTransaction, with storage work between transactions

  1. Resolve approved dictionary/provenance evidence, upload exact bounded source bytes, then record a new immutable manifest.
  2. Provider Posts uses retained qualification bytes; standard People currently has its separate governed synthetic path.
  3. Select due source manifests, delete/confirm storage absence, then append source deletion evidence. Database timestamps preserve microseconds.
Boundary / failure behavior

Source retention is 30 days and is separate from generated objects. Current source-ingestion upload→manifest failure has an orphan-reconciliation gap; 0064 generated-download cleanup does not cover the source prefix.

Walkthrough 15 · dhumi_operator

Generated download cleanup

Database eligibility claim → receipt/ETag-conditional storage delete

  1. Inventory only the generated sample-download prefix within bounded scan/delete limits.
  2. Lock/recheck the exact authorization/object identity. Failed reservations may be cleaned immediately, abandoned ones after 1 hour, authorized ones only after signed expiry+1 hour.
  3. Delete only under the checked receipt/ETag. Preserve protected or uncertain objects and all authorization/idempotency/audit evidence.
Boundary / failure behavior

This maintenance creates no provider work. Historical local scheduling is every 15 minutes with overlap prevention and failure monitoring; current task state/cloud scheduling was not inspected for this atlas.

Walkthrough 16 · dhumi_customer_api / dhumi_operator

Enquiries, qualification and release are separate

Tenant enquiry / private qualification / explicit controlled publication

  1. An enquiry only creates/replays a Tenant-owned received record; the operator later marks contacted/closed with audit.
  2. Qualification prepares an immutable request, binds explicit spend authorization, claims one submission, then records retained execution/poll/result receipts.
  3. Amazon publication advances an approved pointer. Marketplace M10 registers a disabled candidate; People contact contracts record evidence-pending choices, not fulfillment.
Boundary / failure behavior

Provider POSTs belong to a separately authorized operator/application step, never this documentation or SQL alone. Payment/entitlement tables, webhook admission and protected M10 activation are deferred work.

app.due_response_envelopes Protected view

Owner-filtered due API-key recovery-envelope projection for the janitor. Its five columns hide identity, actor fingerprints, request hash and idempotency keys; its base owner policy admits both live and destroyed transition states while the view selects only due live envelopes.

Migrations — forward-only history through 0069

All 69 local SQL source files are explained below. The live object catalogue and local source checksums were observed, but the restricted account could not read the applied ledger.

Bootstrap is separate

Manual administrator bootstrap creates/prepares the database, empty app schema, NOLOGIN owner/capabilities and dedicated environment LOGINs. Migration 0001 fails closed if those boundaries are missing or unsafe; it does not repair/create cluster runtime credentials.

Bootstrap instructions

One transaction per pending file

The runner sorts migration filenames, hashes each file, refuses an existing-version checksum mismatch, skips matching ledger entries, and applies each pending SQL file together with its ledger insert using psql's single-transaction / ON_ERROR_STOP mode. Earlier completed files remain applied if a later file fails.

Migration runner · Ledger table

Never “fix” a ledgered migration in place

Add a new forward migration. Immutable Template/Service/sample history must not be rewritten. DDL activation, operator publication/promotion, worker rollout and feature availability are separate steps. Applying 0056 does not activate customer Marketplace export; 0063 does not enable contact fulfillment; 0064 is generated-download cleanup, not source-sample cleanup.

RangeResponsibility
0001–0012Foundation, identity, sessions, API keys and least privilege.
0013–0028Public catalogue, saved Services, Run admission/list/cancel/retry/events/results.
0029–0044Durable fencing/reconciliation, protected provider execution, Amazon qualification/release, usage and persisted polling.
0045–0053Marketplace private imports, governed samples, preview/download/enquiry and offline adapter boundary.
0054–0056Explicitly bounded qualification, retained execution evidence and disabled export candidate.
0057–0063Posts provider sample lineage, standard People metadata/synthetic preview, contact evidence contract.
0064–0065Generated-download cleanup and legacy synthetic-fixture compatibility.
0066–0069Shared scraper processing identity, private draft staging, exact release dispatch and fail-closed commercial capacity.

No migrations match.

First retained SQL comment lines

Demo Production Phase 1 application-schema foundation.

Cluster roles, the database and the empty app schema are prepared manually
by scripts/bootstrap. This migration fails closed instead of creating or
repairing those security boundaries. PostgreSQL 18 provides
gen_random_uuid() in core, so no pgcrypto extension is required here.
The API resolves a tenant before opening a transaction, then calls
SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = '<uuid>'. An unset context deliberately resolves
to NULL, making every tenant RLS policy return zero rows.

First retained SQL comment lines

Canonical Demo Production data model.

UUIDs are internal primary keys. Public API serialization is responsible for
Dhumi public identifiers; this schema never uses provider identifiers as
customer-facing IDs. Provider references are encrypted/fingerprinted only.
Global catalogue, adapter, evidence and private provider configuration.
Tenant-owned Services and their immutable versions.
Customer-visible work. The exact provider execution configuration is pinned
at admission, never resolved from whichever mapping is active later.
Idempotency is authoritative in PostgreSQL. Signup records intentionally
have no tenant yet; authenticated mutations always have one.
Updated timestamps are database-derived, not trusted from an application.

Least-privilege database boundary for the response-envelope janitor.

This migration intentionally does not create cluster LOGIN/capability roles,
define deployment scheduling, alter the ten-minute recovery promise, or
grant access to request identity, actor fingerprints or idempotency keys.
The table owner is already a trusted migration principal. These policies
let its protected view transition exactly one envelope state while FORCE
ROW LEVEL SECURITY remains enabled on the base table.
PostgreSQL applies a SELECT policy as a new-row visibility check during an
UPDATE. A direct janitor table policy therefore cannot both hide destroyed
tombstones and transition a live row into that hidden state. The
owner-filtered view resolves that conflict: its base-table policy accepts
both transition states, while the view exposes only live due envelopes and
only the row identifier and four envelope columns needed for destruction.

Pattern 4 resilience: durable reconciliation after uncertain execution.

A queue redelivery must not repeat a cost-incurring submission after a Run
has left QUEUED. This migration converts that uncertainty into one durable,
Run-only jobs.reconcile command and makes reconciliation completion an
atomic, fenced PostgreSQL operation.
Idempotency belongs to the exact dead-lettered event, not permanently to the
Run. A recovery command can itself reach the DLQ; after that published
command is repaired, the operator must be able to create a new recovery
command without allowing concurrent pending commands for the same Run.
Operator recovery never republishes a broker message directly. It creates
one new durable Run-only outbox command. The normal dispatcher and Job
Manager then apply the same Tenant lookup, claim and fencing rules as every
other delivery. A terminal Run needs no replay and is reported as such.

First retained SQL comment lines

PostgreSQL-owned timestamp authority for LinkedIn People sample ingestion.

The provider metadata observation is stored with PostgreSQL microsecond
precision, while JavaScript Date values have millisecond precision. Passing
the observation timestamp through JavaScript therefore cannot preserve an
exact equality boundary. This forward-only correction keeps migration 0061
immutable and makes PostgreSQL pass its retained source timestamp directly
into the existing fail-closed recorder.

Handover — what the next developer or AI must know

Use this as an orientation map, then inspect linked source/tests. Installed schema is evidence of structure, not proof of active-use frequency, complete regression, cloud deployment, or commercial readiness.

Keep these invariants

  • Resolve authenticated Tenant/actor/scopes before Tenant repository work; do not accept arbitrary Tenant overrides.
  • Use the fixed transaction seams; never run the API/workers as postgres or dhumi_owner.
  • Preserve immutable Template, Service, adapter, mapping and sample pins/history.
  • Use expected state revisions, row locks and live Attempt fences; do not directly update Run state to force success.
  • Provider continuation/resource IDs stay encrypted/fingerprinted; object keys/verifiers stay private.
  • Do not automatically repeat an ambiguous billable POST. Reconcile retained evidence/continuation.
  • Outbox, Artifact, usage and audit evidence have different jobs; do not collapse them merely because the schema feels large.
  • All 97 observed foreign keys use ON DELETE RESTRICT. Plan explicit, evidence-preserving lifecycle/cleanup rather than assuming cascades.

Meaning of “complete”

  • Stored-sample preview/query/bounded download is not full-provider search or paid export.
  • Posts provider sample lineage is governed local-demo evidence with a formal-agreement gate; do not silently treat an interim reference as final rights approval.
  • Standard People synthetic preview is distinct from real provider-derived People/contact fulfillment.
  • Contact choices are database-backed, but disabled fulfillment stays disabled until exact endpoint/payload/entitlement/semantics/rights/qualification/mapping proof.
  • MPayment decisions, orders, signed webhooks, Tenant entitlement, refunds/reconciliation, versioned spend limits and atomic paid admission remain separate work.
  • M10's disabled candidate is not a customer release; never enable it solely because the rows/functions exist.
  • The shared scraper schema is installed, but no new retailer is customer-published. Target still needs a protected mapping, commercial evidence, independent qualification, publication and deliberate default-off worker opt-in.
  • Cloud storage, identities/RBAC/networking, retention scheduling and production proof are not established by this local atlas.

Collector, coverage and maintenance notes.

Safe metadata query — SQL editor or psql

Catalogue inspection does not need customer row queries or psql backslash commands. Use the intended restricted connection.

BEGIN READ ONLY;
SELECT current_database(), current_user,
       current_setting('server_version') AS postgres_version;
SELECT c.relname AS table_name, c.relrowsecurity AS rls,
       c.relforcerowsecurity AS force_rls
FROM pg_catalog.pg_class AS c
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace AS n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
WHERE n.nspname = 'app' AND c.relkind IN ('r', 'p')
ORDER BY c.relname;
ROLLBACK;

Equivalent catalogue checks were exercised by the collector. A ROLLBACK without BEGIN only produces a warning; it is not evidence that prior validation passed.

Every observed table (43), table column (606), function (120), protected view (1) and local migration source (69) has an explanation/source path. Index/trigger/policy/permission details are included; dependencies/callers are explicitly heuristic.
